This abbreviated nestling phase is characteristic of many tropical forest birds, which face high nest predation risk.

These mass values represent the asymptotic size reached after skeletal growth ceases, and they appear to be maintained throughout the reproductive lifespan with only minor seasonal fluctuation linked to fat deposition during the wet season.
